It fires on diverse content types including numbers, proper nouns, technical terms, and common words, suggesting a general end-of-sequence or completion signal rather than a specific semantic theme.
candidate_explanation: Often activates on the token immediately before text beginning with K or k, including within words, names, code and quantities. Examples include DIS before K in DISK, 4 before K in 4K, and honky-ton before the final k. Activation belongs to the preceding word fragment, digit, space or punctuation, rather than necessarily to K itself. Some activations have non-K continuations, so this is a frequent pattern, not an exclusive rule.
